Install with two commands (claude plugin marketplace add, then claude plugin install lemo-opuscar@lemolab), needs Node 20+, ffmpeg and Python 3.11+. author: adonisautomates

title: Auto-clipping a viral video with Ssemble
author: itsvera.clips
key_info: The reel is a 7-step screen demo of Ssemble: pick a viral YouTube video (it uses a MrBeast video), paste the link, click 'get shorts', pick the best generated clip and schedule it to a connected account, 'in under 45 seconds'. The steps match what is shown on screen. It says nothing about permission to reuse the video: clipping someone else's content for your own channel is not licensed by the tool, and YouTube's reused-content rules apply. The post ends with a 'Comment INFO' lead magnet and the caption 'This should be illegal' is clickbait.

title: Harness2 reopen-your-files rule for agents
author: simplyaishow
key_info: Harness2 (google-research/harness2) is a real open-source framework from Google Cloud AI Research that has a stronger model rewrite the prompts, guardrails and scripts around an agent without retraining it; coverage names Gemini 3.5 Flash as an agent and Claude Opus 4.8 as the editor. The reel's 43 to 78 score is described by the creator as one of the best examples, and the average gain is smaller (coverage reports up to about 11 points per step on benchmarks). The tip itself is practical and free: tell your agent to reopen every file it made and check that numbers match before it says it is done.

title: Claude Code watch skill with Gemini
author: lindsay.ai
key_info: The method is real: the open-source claude-video repo (bradautomates/claude-video, MIT) adds a /watch skill that turns a video link into timestamped frames and a transcript, and can send YouTube links straight to the Gemini API when you set a Gemini API key. The on-screen Google docs page shows YouTube URL input is a free preview feature whose pricing and limits may change. The 'agent framework' for client agents and the guide are not named and sit behind a comment-for-DM funnel.

title: AI influencer motion control workflow demo
author: tech_new_trends
key_info: A screen demo of an AI-influencer workflow: a node-graph (ComfyUI-style, shown on RunningHub AI) swaps a model's face into generated portraits and then runs a 'Motion Control' job that animated one image into a dance video in about 16 minutes. No steps, settings or models are explained, and the 'full workflow with guides' is behind a link or Telegram group. Nothing here could be checked beyond what is on screen. Note the content is photoreal AI personas built by face-swapping.

title: Code Mode instead of classic MCP
author: saurabhs.builds
key_info: Same story as an earlier reel (see the Cloudflare Code Mode note): Cloudflare's Code Mode and Anthropic's code-execution-with-MCP pattern are real. Anthropic's post reports 150,000 tokens down to 2,000 (98.7%) for one example, but that is a single scenario and one independent test found about 77%. The 'companies are moving away from MCP' framing is overstated, since the code still calls MCP servers. A TL;DR and alternatives are in 'Your instruction'.

title: VoiceStudio open-source voice cloning
author: aiwithdivyam
key_info: VoiceStudio (debpalash/VoiceStudio) is a real open-source (AGPL-3.0) app for voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription and audiobooks, with 646 languages claimed. The repo showed about 80k stars (the reel says 79k). It runs locally on your machine (GPU or slower CPU); remote services are optional. Not confirmed: the '10 seconds of audio' for cloning and a flat 'no data ever leaves' claim. Link is only given by DM.

title: Rumble monetization with view-exchange app
author: startupgully
key_info: The reel shows a Rumble dashboard with $7.90 earned, 120 views and 276 followers, and the creator admits these views are 'not organic': they come from an app where users watch each other's videos. Rumble is reported to have no follower or watch-hour minimum for basic monetization, unlike YouTube, but the earnings shown are tiny and exchange-driven, and a guide plus app link are offered only by DM after a comment (lead-magnet funnel). Whether this complies with Rumble's rules was not confirmed.

title: Four risky websites for phones and OTPs
author: briefonlive
key_info: The reel misdescribes the sites. NumLookup is a reverse phone lookup service, not a way to call people without showing your number. SMS24 and YOPmail are public disposable number and email inboxes: real, but anyone can read the messages, and many apps block them. The fourth site is a call and SMS bombing tool, which is harassment and should not be used on anyone's phone. The caption itself adds safety disclaimers the voiceover lacks. Do not use these for banking, sensitive accounts or anything you need to recover.

title: Faceless channel on trending Netflix shows
author: scottsmithyta
key_info: The viewership figure is close to reported data (Monster: The Ed Gein Story debuted with about 12.2M views, over roughly three days rather than four). The $3,078 monthly earnings of an unnamed 'small channel' and the cost of about $75 per video are the creator's own claims with no channel or proof shown. The post ends with a 'Comment Training' lead magnet. The three prompts were on slides that were not captured.

title: Open-source Higgsfield AI alternative
author: futureproof_hacks
key_info: The repo is real: an MIT-licensed open-source image and video generation studio (Open Generative AI by Anil-matcha, about 31k stars when checked), and the reel shows a fork (Autom8AI/Open-Higgsfield-AI) rebranded as a Higgsfield alternative. The software is free, but 'unlimited videos for free' is misleading: cloud generation goes through a third-party API (Muapi in the original, kie.ai in the fork's commit messages) that needs an API key and has its own pricing, and local generation needs a capable GPU. Link was only given via bio or DM.

title: Cloudflare Code Mode MCP explained
author: decoding_tech_
key_info: Cloudflare's Code Mode is real: its MCP server exposes the whole Cloudflare API through two tools (search and execute), where the model writes code instead of calling many tool definitions, which Cloudflare says takes about 1,000 tokens against about 1.17 million for an equivalent standard MCP server. The 'companies are moving away from MCP' headline is overstated: Code Mode still runs as an MCP server, so it optimises MCP rather than replacing it. 'Other companies are following' was not checked.

title: 80GB A100 GPU via Google AI Pro Colab
author: microtech.india
key_info: The reel (a repost of @baljeet.ai) says you can get an 80GB-VRAM GPU 'for free'. Its own screenshot shows what is real: a Google Gemma post saying Google AI Pro plans now include premium Colab benefits with A100 80GB GPUs (Ultra even H100s), enough to run Gemma 4 31B in bf16, fine-tune Gemma 4 E4B in bf16, and LoRA/QLoRA the 26B and 31B models. It is a paid plan, not free; the narration adds a 30 to 45 percent discount for 1.5 years that was not verified.

author: eliteoptionstrader2
key_info: Trader says stocks, AI names, gold, crypto and banks fell together after US CPI hit 3.7%, the dollar index jumped and money moved to cash. title: ComfyUI for local AI media
author: justinmendez.ai
key_info: ComfyUI is a real, free, open-source node-based engine for image, video and audio generation that runs on your own hardware, so there are no per-generation credits. The '5.6 million downloads' figure could not be confirmed, and you need a capable GPU for the heavy models.

author: dailydoseofds_
key_info: Understand Anything is a real open-source (MIT) plugin that builds an interactive knowledge graph of a codebase with a multi-agent pipeline, with commands such as /understand and /understand-dashboard. The repo showed about 87k GitHub stars when checked, consistent with the post's 86k+. The repo link was in the comments, which were not fetched; install steps are in the repo README.

author: himanshhh.ai
key_info: A reel naming three AI video generators as free: MiniMax, Hailuo and Tencent's Hunyuan. All three have some free access, but the limits are small, watermarked or hardware-heavy, and the tool names in the audio are partly garbled.

title: Clipping and copyright: is it safe
author: tillmann_clips
key_info: Half right: clipping for a paid campaign (Whop or Ssemble Clip Rewards) is the safe route because the owner authorises and pays for clips. But 'copyright has never been an issue' and 'just tag the creator' are not safe advice: YouTube's reused-content rules reward meaningful transformation, and credit does not by itself make reused material monetizable or licensed. The creator also promotes the tool with a discount code (TJ10) that earns them commission.

title: Emergent: sell AI-built apps to SMBs
author: casarthakahuja
key_info: Funding facts check out: Emergent, run by twin brothers Mukund and Madhav Jha, raised a $130M Series C at a $1.5B valuation. The pitch that you can learn the tool and sell custom software to small businesses is a plausible business idea but unproven: no income evidence is given, the Rs 10,000 to 80,000 website and store prices are the creator's own figures, and the post is marked #collab, so it is a paid promotion.

title: Free alternatives to paid AI tools
author: max_v.v
key_info: Two presenters pair paid AI tools with free ones (video: ArtFlow, voice cloning: FishAudio vs ElevenLabs, brainstorming: Gemini). All three free tiers exist but are limited, and the full list of 46 is behind a comment-for-DM gate.

title: Arnold on the best tricep exercise
